info.title: db-lens
info.description: A read-only command-line analyzer for Microsoft SQL Server: ranks queries by what they cost the server, shows execution plans, inventories indexes with their real usage, and reports unused, duplicate, redundant and missing indexes — plus wait statistics, live blocking chains, statistics freshness and deadlock history. Emits a stable JSON contract or a table. Never writes to your database.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
db-lens 0.0.0-alpha.0.3 — read-only MSSQL query and index analyzer.

Reads query statistics (Query Store or plan cache), index inventory and usage, and
execution plans; reports unused, duplicate and missing indexes. Every statement it
runs is a SELECT over system views — it never issues DDL or DML. Suggested changes
are printed as T-SQL for you to review.

Output is a stable JSON envelope when stdout is not a terminal, so the tool composes
with scripts and agents; use --format to choose explicitly.

Required permissions: VIEW SERVER STATE on the instance, VIEW DATABASE STATE per database.

commands.name: queries
commands.description:
Rank queries by how much they cost the server.

Reads Query Store when the target databases have it enabled, and the plan cache otherwise;
the envelope's "source" field always says which. Each row carries the plan id to hand to
'dblens plan', so the ranking and the plan investigation chain together.

options.description: How many queries to return. Defaults to 25. [default: 25]

options.name: --order-by

commands.name: query
commands.description:
Show one query in full: its text, its aggregate cost, and every plan behind it.

More than one plan row means the optimizer chose differently at some point; compare the
average duration per plan to tell a harmless recompile from a regression, then pass the
plan id to 'dblens plan'.

commands.name: plan
commands.description:
Show the execution plan behind a plan id.

The operator tree is flattened with indentation, so it reads the same as a table, as CSV
and as JSON. Cost % is the operator's own cost with its children subtracted, which is
what "the expensive operator" actually means. Missing indexes and optimizer warnings the
plan carries are reported alongside it.

options.name: --raw-xml
options.description: Emit the ShowplanXML unchanged. With -o plan.sqlplan the file opens in SSMS or Azure Data Studio. [default: False]

options.name: --all-statements
options.description: Show every statement in the plan. By default only the costliest one is shown, which is what a procedure plan is usually about. [default: False]

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: Query Store plan_id (a number) or a plan_handle (0x..., a leading prefix is enough).

commands.name: indexes
commands.description:
List indexes with their definition, size and usage.

Usage counters accumulate since the instance started, so the result carries a warning
whenever uptime is too short to support a conclusion. An index with no row at all in
sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats is reported as having no data rather than zero reads -- the
difference is what separates a safe drop from an outage.

options.name: --top
options.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 100. [default: 100]

options.name: --order-by
options.description: Ranking metric. One of: size, reads, writes, rows, name. [default: Size]

options.name: --schema
options.description: Only objects in this schema (exact match).

options.name: --table
options.description: Only tables whose name contains this text.

options.name: --name
options.description: Only indexes whose name contains this text.

options.name: --min-size-mb
options.description: Skip indexes smaller than this many megabytes.

options.name: --include-heaps
options.description: Include heaps (tables with no clustered index) in the inventory. [default: False]

options.name: --min-uptime-days
options.description: Days of instance uptime required before "never read" counts as evidence rather than noise. [default: 7]

commands.name: unused
commands.description:
Find indexes nothing reads but every write maintains.

Usage counters reset when the instance restarts, and an index with no row in the usage DMV
has not been observed at all rather than observed idle. Both cases are reported at Info
severity: still worth reviewing, not safe to act on from this evidence alone. Raise the bar
with --min-uptime-days, or relax what counts as unused with --max-reads and --min-writes.

options.description: How many rows to return. Defaults to 100. [default: 100]

options.name: --order-by

options.name: --max-reads

options.name: --min-writes
options.description: An unread index is only worth dropping if it costs at least this many writes to maintain. [default: 1]

commands.name: duplicates
commands.description:
Find indexes another index already covers.

Reports exact duplicates (same keys, same includes, same filter) and redundant indexes whose
keys are a leading prefix of a wider index that also covers their included columns. This
needs no usage data -- a duplicate is redundant by its definition -- so a recently restarted
instance does not weaken the result. Unique indexes and constraint-backing indexes are never
proposed for removal.

commands.name: missing
commands.description:
List the indexes the optimizer wished existed, ranked by estimated impact.

These come straight from the missing-index DMVs, which never account for the write cost
of an index and never notice that an existing index almost covers the need. Treat them
as candidates; 'dblens indexes suggest' reconciles them against what is already there.

commands.name: suggest
commands.description:
Every index finding at once: unused, duplicate, redundant, missing, widenable, unindexed
foreign keys and disabled indexes.

Missing-index recommendations are reconciled against what already exists -- ones an index
already serves are dropped, and where an existing index only needs to be wider that is what
is proposed, rather than a second index on the same leading column.

With -o fixes.sql the findings are written as a reviewable T-SQL script instead of a table.

commands.name: stats
commands.description:
Find statistics the optimizer should no longer trust.

Reports statistics whose modification counter has passed the auto-update threshold
(stale), old statistics with churn below it (nothing will ever refresh them), NORECOMPUTE
flags, and thin samples on large tables. Stale statistics are the usual cause behind
skewed row estimates -- if queries here show QRY006 findings, this is where to look.

Suggested UPDATE STATISTICS commands are printed for review, never executed.

options.name: --top
options.description: How many findings to return, worst first. Defaults to 50. [default: 50]

options.name: --stale-days
options.description: Report statistics older than this many days when rows have changed underneath them. [default: 30]

commands.name: waits
commands.description:
What the server has been waiting on since it started.

Reads the cumulative wait statistics (sys.dm_os_wait_stats; the database-scoped
equivalent on Azure SQL Database) with the benign background waits filtered out, and
reports the profile: CPU pressure, parallelism, buffer IO, locking, memory grants and
log writes each get a finding when their share is high enough to matter.

The counters accumulate from instance start, so this answers "what does this server
wait on" -- for "what is blocking right now", use: dblens blocking.

options.name: --top
options.description: How many wait types to return, ranked by total wait time. Defaults to 25. [default: 25]

commands.name: blocking
commands.description:
Who is blocking whom, right now.

Takes one snapshot of every active request plus every idle session that still holds an
open transaction — the classic invisible head blocker — and reports the chains: which
session sits at the head, how many others are queued behind it, and idle transactions
whose locks outlive their work.

This is a point-in-time picture. An empty result means nothing was blocked at this
instant, not that blocking never happens; for the cumulative view, use: dblens waits.

options.name: --long-running-minutes
options.description: Report an unblocked request as long-running past this many minutes. [default: 5]

commands.name: deadlocks
commands.description:
Recent deadlocks, from the system_health Extended Events session.

SQL Server has been recording every deadlock there since 2012 — no trace flag, no
setup. Each event is parsed into who fought over what: the victim, both statements,
the contested objects and lock modes. When the same objects keep deadlocking, that
repetition is reported as its own finding, because a recurring pattern is a design
problem rather than bad luck.

Reads the server's .xel files, so the result is capped by --top. Not available on
Azure SQL Database (no file target there); works on box installs and Managed Instance.

options.name: --top
options.description: How many of the most recent deadlock events to read. Defaults to 20. [default: 20]

commands.name: report
commands.description:
Run every check at once and report what was found.

Ranks the costliest queries, analyzes the plan behind each, adds the full index and
statistics analysis, and reads the server diagnostics: wait profile, current blocking,
and recent deadlocks. Sections a login or edition cannot answer degrade to warnings.

With --format markdown the result is a written report; with --format json it is the same
data structured, which is the form to hand to another tool.

options.name: --skip-queries
options.description: Report only on indexes and diagnostics. Useful where no statistics source is available. [default: False]

options.name: --skip-diagnostics
options.description: Skip the waits, blocking and deadlock sections. [default: False]

commands.name: schema
commands.description:
Print the JSON Schema of the shapes db-lens returns.

Generated from the types that do the serializing, so it describes the real output rather
than a hand-written copy of it. Every command wraps its result in the envelope; the
per-command data field carries the shapes listed here.

arguments.name: TYPE
arguments.description: Which shape to describe: envelope, error, query-stat, query-plan-stat, index, missing-index, finding, plan-statement, plan-node. Omit for all of them.

options.name: --default
options.description: Use this profile when neither --profile nor $DBLENS_CONNECTION_STRING is set. [default: False]
